notes: P50/P95/P99 summarize the recorded sample population, not confidence intervals. Missing data is never replaced with zero.
Budgets: frameMs=not supplied; cpuMemoryMiB=not supplied; vramMiB=not supplied
Production input purpose=validation; scheduling diagnostics=on; app diagnostic sink=True. Validation and performance populations are not mixed.

Production: 4 passed measured processes; 0 prewarm/failed/incomplete records excluded from latency comparisons. Frames are correlated within a process; per-process quantiles are plotted individually, never pooled as independent experiments.
Production worker limits: [4]; W labels identify each limit. No results are averaged across different worker limits, blocks or executable candidates.
A TaskGraph/DAG critical path is unavailable unless dependency-linked task intervals are separately recorded. Inclusive profiler scope durations alone do not establish that path.
No dependency-linked TaskGraph intervals inside a measured frame window: DAG completion-chain plots unavailable. Diagnostic sink runs are separate from performance-off captures.

figures.title: Production frame distributions by process/block
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. legacy: 2 processes, shared: 2 processes. Every marker is one process quantile of its measured frames; P95/P99 are not confidence bounds. Missing GPU data is unavailable, not zero. No frame budget was supplied.

figures.title: Production recorded frame time series, page 1
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. Every recorded frame is shown in its own process, with common y limits across all pages; no smoothing, interpolation, rebasing or cross-process concatenation. Shading uses the runner's explicit measuredFrameRange when available; absent windows are not guessed. The per-process Raw.frameMs distribution remains the measured-window authority.

figures.title: Production CPU scope wall durations
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. legacy: 2 processes, shared: 2 processes; each dot is one process's scope-occurrence median, which may have a different sample count than frameCount. Top 16 paths ranked by their largest process median. Nested, parallel and idle scopes can overlap; no scope durations are summed, subtracted into CPU work, or relabeled as a critical path.

figures.title: Production non-overlapping coordinator frame path
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. Only explicit producer-contracted intervals are used, with non-overlap/envelope validation. Stacks use means from the same complete frames, not sums of P50s. Unattributed frame envelope is a measured duration difference, not worker idle or useful CPU work. This is not a reconstructed TaskGraph longest path.

figures.title: Production memory and process-thread peaks
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. legacy: 2 processes, shared: 2 processes; one marker per available process metric. OS high-waters include startup only through the last successful sample; current-value sampled peaks depend on poll cadence/window. Device-local allocated/block/usage measures are not additive or automatically process-private. Missing values remain absent. No RAM/VRAM budget is assumed when none is supplied; whole-device capacity is not an application budget.

figures.title: Production RHI allocation high-waters
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. Event high-waters are simultaneous totals maintained at RHI allocation/free events, through the last queried snapshot. They cover RHI-tracked allocations, excluding untracked external SDK/driver memory. Current-value sampled maxima are separate. Host+device totals are not VRAM-only; domains and these totals are not added together. Missing counters remain unavailable.

figures.title: Production CPU occupancy
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. Each available marker is process CPU time divided by lifetime wall time, across all process threads. It includes loading/warmup when those fall in the producer's process window. It is neither worker utilization nor a CPU usage peak. No host-wide CPU utilization or peak CPU usage is synthesized.

figures.title: Production domain allocation peaks
figures.caption: VALIDATION telemetry — not a performance A/B or FPS result. Each point is one process's reported peak for that allocation domain. Peaks can occur on different frames. RHI domains may include host and device allocations; this is not a VRAM-only partition. Domain definitions and ownership come from the producer; they are not summed into a simultaneous total or a memory budget.
